notes: Drive Health now reads real SMART through USB enclosures. Standard Windows queries can't see an NVMe SSD's health through a USB-to-NVMe bridge, so a worn drive in a caddy used to fall back to placeholder data. The tool now tunnels the drive's actual NVMe SMART/Health log through the common bridge chips — ASMedia, Realtek and JMicron — using the same vendor commands smartmontools uses, so a Kioxia (or any NVMe) in a dock reports its true wear/health just like it would connected internally. Each reading is validated (an unsupported bridge can't fake a pristine drive), and if a bridge genuinely can't be read it still shows the honest 'connect the drive directly' message from the previous update rather than a false 100%. The card shows where the reading came from (e.g. 'Live NVMe SMART via USB bridge (ASMedia)').
